title: Mathlib v4.30 source proposition Nat.Abundant.mul_left
statement: The proposition declared as `Nat.Abundant.mul_left` in the pinned Mathlib v4.30 source.

evidence.supports: Abundant n -> Not (Eq m zero) -> Abundant (mul m n)
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- abundant_mul_left 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.abundant_mul_left[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: A direct instance of `Nat.sum_divisors_scale_le` (`divisor_sum_scale.rs`) at scale factor `q := m`: `m * sumDivisors n <= sumDivisors (m*n)`. Multiplies the `Abundant n` hypothesis through by `m` (`Nat.mul_lt_mul_left`'s `mpr` direction) to get `Lt (mul m (mul 2 n)) (sumDivisors (mul m n))`, then reassociates `mul m (mul 2 n)` to `mul 2 (mul m n)` via `mul_comm`/`mul_assoc`.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat prelude's trusted surface is empty
evidence.notes: nat_axiom_inventory --require-axiom-free nat enumerates the built Nat environment and exits non-zero unless it admits no Axiom, Opaque or Quotient declaration. A theorem cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain, so an empty trusted surface bounds every individual theorem's footprint by [].

provenance.source: statement-only extraction of the Mathlib proposition from Mathlib v4.30.0 (see prior_art), independently proved here through Kernel::add_declaration

prior_art.attribution: the proposition was read from the pinned statement-only inventory; the proof term and tactic trace were not consulted

notes: abundant_deficient_lemmas.rs closed seven ml430 mirrors and left this one open for missing divisor-sum-monotonicity infrastructure (not a divergence question -- Mathlib's `Abundant` and this kernel's `Lt (mul 2 n) (sumDivisors n)` are the same characterization, per that module's revised verdict). Closed here by `Nat.sum_divisors_scale_le` (`divisor_sum_scale.rs`): scaling every divisor of `n` by a positive `m` injects into the divisors of `m*n`, built as a `sumRange` reindexing induction over the same index range `mul_sumRange` (`algebra.rs`) exposes.
